subject.title: Feat: Add Trivy SBOM and vulnerability scanning to Docker release

question: Should Docker release publishing add Trivy SBOM/SARIF scanning with Code Scanning write permission, setup-trivy execution/cache, and a fixed-critical vulnerability gate once current-head official-path proof is available?
rationale: This changes the trusted release workflow permission boundary, third-party code execution/cache path, Code Scanning uploads, and release-blocking policy, which automation cannot safely approve as a line-level repair.

options.title: Require proof and owner approval
options.body: Ask for current-head redacted release logs/artifacts covering GHCR and Docker Hub, then require release/security owner approval before merge.

options.title: Accept release-pipeline risk
options.body: A release/security owner can explicitly accept the partial proof and own the scanner, permission, cache, and fixed-critical gate risk for this version.

options.title: Pause for owner-led design
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers want Docker release scanning introduced through a broader release-hardening plan instead of this PR.

recommendation.title: Require proof and owner approval
recommendation.body: Ask for current-head redacted release logs/artifacts covering GHCR and Docker Hub, then require release/security owner approval before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent Docker release workflow and Docker Hub publishing history is the strongest owner signal for this release-security decision.
